items.title: Southwest Airlines Slashes 2026 Profit Guidance on Higher Fuel Bills
items.summary: Southwest is the latest airline to slash its profit outlook for the year as surging fuel costs bite into record revenues.

items.title: United’s Higher Fares Can’t Keep Up With Soaring Fuel Costs
items.summary: Yes, United is struggling to keep pace with soaring fuel costs, but CEO Scott Kirby thinks its rivals have even bigger problems ahead.

items.title: Hilton Bets on Scandic to Crack Nordics
items.summary: International hotel brands have struggled to gain scale in the Nordic market. This deal shows one way to do it: letting someone who already knows the market carry most of the risk.

items.title: Airbnb’s New Policy for Hosts: Don’t Ask Guests to Wash Dishes or Strip Beds
items.summary: The new policy formalizes a lot of things Airbnb has been pushing hosts to avoid as unreasonable in recent years — and thus it comes with more enforcement bite.

items.title: Corporate Travel to Saudi Arabia Freezes as Riyadh Airport Stays Restricted
items.summary: Houthi strikes have cut Riyadh off from scheduled flights and pushed the kingdom’s events season into 2027. The longer the closure lasts, the harder it gets for Saudi Arabia to sell itself as a reliable host for business tourism.

items.title: Real-Time Personalization: Turning Browsers Into Bookers
items.summary: Real-time personalization can help travel brands earn loyalty without defaulting to broad discounts — but it works only when brands put preference data to use quickly and deliver an experience that matches the marketing promise.

items.title: Poland’s Economic Rise Is Becoming a Travel Story Worth Watching
items.summary: More Polish households can afford to travel, and airlines, hotel owners, and lenders are backing additional capacity.

items.title: Why the Best Corporate Travel Strategy Isn’t Just About Spending Less
items.summary: New ASTA and GBTA research suggests companies should evaluate corporate travel in relation to business performance, not simply as a cost line. Mark Meader of ASTA explains how benchmarking, policy flexibility, and travel management can help companies invest more strategically.
